data.narrative:
Tevel Aerobotics is a Series B-stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Yaniv Maor that has raised $42.6M to date. The Drones & Autonomous sector includes 8 private peers (Elroy Air, Waymo, Wayave, Zipline, Joby Aviation and others) and no public comparables, limiting the breadth of valuation anchors available.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is applicable. Using $42.6M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy, a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-later-stage progression implies a valuation of $81M. This reflects the pattern that Series B investors typically deploy capital at valuations roughly 1.9x prior rounds in this sector. The peer-median approach could not be applied: while seven same-sector peers exist, fewer than three comparable datapoints were available at identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier, making a filtered peer multiple unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $69M (low) to $93M (high), centered on $81M. The primary uncertainty is the narrow methodological foundation—reliance on a single step-up multiplier rather than triangulation across market, income, or robust peer approaches. Additional uncertainty stems from sparse public and near-peer private data in autonomous systems at this exact stage and capital deployment level. Revenue traction, customer concentration, and pathway to Series C fundraising dynamics would refine this range materially.
